PullRequest.Title: chore: use new pools for publish runs
PullRequest.Body: Applies only to main and release/* branches. It also does not apply to sanity test jobs.

Scenarios.Scenario: Scheduled or manually queued publish-enabled product build on main/release/*, with the default Windows, Linux, Alpine, Web, Quality, Copilot, Publish, source-analysis, and APIScan work
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Platform build jobs and artifact publication remain the pipeline's critical path; release, when enabled, waits for Publish and ApproveRelease. The diff only selects dedicated Windows/Linux agent pools before these unchanged jobs execute.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: build/azure-pipelines/product-build.yml:181-191 and pool assignments throughout the changed stages
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Allocate an Azure Pipelines agent for each eligible Windows/Linux job from the new publishing pool
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One allocation per existing job; effective job cardinality is unchanged, with multiple independent jobs queued in parallel for a default product build.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same jobs and concurrency requested agents from 1es-windows-2022-x64 or 1es-ubuntu-22.04-x64.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Agent queueing precedes every affected job, but there is no repository evidence that the dedicated pools have lower capacity or slower machines, so a queue-time regression is not established.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Restore dependencies/caches, fetch secrets and toolchains, upload build artifacts/CDN data, and publish processed artifacts
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing per-job operations across the unchanged build matrix; cache hits continue to suppress the same dependency-install work.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical network operations ran on the legacy pools with the same per-job cardinality and ordering.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These calls remain on each job's build/publish path, but the diff neither adds calls nor increases retries, payloads, or item fan-out.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run npm, gulp, Rust compilation, archive, signing, Docker, and platform build commands
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing fixed command sequences per matrix job; no command or loop was changed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same subprocesses ran in the same jobs on the prior default pools.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Compilation and packaging dominate job runtime, but their placement and multiplicity are unchanged; only their agent pool is parameterized.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The default matrix has two Windows CLI jobs, three Linux CLI jobs, four Alpine jobs, one Web job, the full platform builds, and independent quality/security/publish jobs. Template expansion and job count are unchanged by the diff.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Stages with dependsOn: [] can queue concurrently, and jobs within those stages retain their prior Azure Pipelines scheduling. The diff changes the target pool for each eligible job but adds no jobs, Promise/task fan-out, limiter, serialization, or dependency edge.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The existing Cache@2 keys, cache-hit branches, artifact reuse, and publish retry/idempotency files are unchanged. Changing the agent pool can affect transient machine warmth, but repository evidence does not establish a persistent cache miss or invalidation mechanism; service-backed cache keys remain the same.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that pool selection changes and that job/boundary cardinality do not; all changed templates and their call sites were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual publishing-pool capacity, machine image warmth, and queue duration are external to the repository. Without evidence that they are worse, these unknowns cannot establish an actionable regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The PR reroutes an unchanged workload to dedicated publishing pools without code evidence of extra work, lower concurrency, cache defeat, or a slower critical path.

Scenarios.Scenario: CI or publish-disabled run, including callers of the parameterized templates from product-build-template.yml and product-build-ado-ci.yml
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The same existing compilation/test jobs remain on the standard pools because VSCODE_USE_PUBLISHING_POOLS is false, while external template callers omit the new optional parameter and receive its legacy default.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: build/azure-pipelines/product-build.yml:181-191 and defaults in the six changed job templates
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One allocation for each pre-existing job.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same jobs used the same standard Windows and Ubuntu pools.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: No change: these scenarios resolve to the exact previous pool names.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing dependency, secret, artifact, signing, and publication-service calls in transitive job templates
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Unchanged per job and per artifact.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical network calls and cache behavior.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: No changed placement or call count.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The job matrix depends on existing build parameters; the new parameter does not alter matrix size or command count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Unchanged stage/job parallelism and dependencies; every added template parameter has a default matching the formerly hard-coded pool.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Unchanged cache services, keys, hit variables, and negative/failure behavior because these runs remain on the original pools.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High; all repository call sites of the changed templates were searched, and omitted parameters use legacy defaults.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material for PR causality: pool names resolve to previous values in this scenario.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance change for CI/publish-disabled and legacy template callers.

Scenarios.Scenario: Sanity test stages following a publish-enabled build
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Published-build sanity tests still wait for Publish; artifact sanity tests still wait for their platform stages. Their explicit poolName values are not replaced by the new variables.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Download published or pipeline artifacts and execute sanity suites
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing fixed matrix by enabled target architecture.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same sanity jobs used their explicit legacy pool names.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Remains after Publish or the relevant build stage; the diff does not move these calls or jobs onto the publishing pools.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The same OS/architecture sanity-test matrix and artifact set as before.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing independent sanity jobs retain their prior pool assignments and dependency structure.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No sanity-test cache, artifact-download, or retry logic was changed.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High; both published and artifact sanity-stage regions were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None relevant to the changed pool routing; sanity pools are explicitly unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression; the stated sanity-test exclusion is preserved.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all seven changed files and every diff page. Traced publishing, non-publishing/CI, template-caller, and sanity-test scenarios; checked agent scheduling, matrix concurrency, caches, subprocesses, filesystem/archive work, and network/artifact boundaries. The change only parameterizes pool names and routes publish-enabled main/release builds to dedicated pools. No high-confidence diff-caused performance regression or provable shipped-regression fix was found.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
